beats.text: Your H100 GPU is idling. Even with FlashAttention-2, you're only hitting 35% utilization. You're paying for a supercar but driving it in a school zone.
beats.visual_focus: A glowing H100 chip with a pulsing red bar at 35% capacity.

visual_blueprint.title: THE H100 BOTTLENECK

motif_params.title: THE H100 BOTTLENECK
motif_params.sub: Current hardware utilization vs theoretical peak

beats.text: Why? Because standard kernels force the same threads to fetch data AND do math. It’s like a chef who stops cooking to run to the grocery store.
beats.visual_focus: Split-screen: One chef running back and forth versus a kitchen line.

beats.text: FlashAttention-3 solves this with warp-specialization. We split the threads: one group acts as a dedicated courier for data, while the others stay locked on math.
beats.visual_focus: Animation showing a 'Warp' splitting into two colors: Blue (Load) and Green (Compute).

visual_blueprint.title: FLASHATTENTION-3 ARCHITECTURE

beats.text: By using the Tensor Memory Accelerator, these couriers move data asynchronously. The math units never wait; they just consume the stream of tensors as they arrive.
beats.visual_focus: TMA unit moving blocks into SMEM while Tensor Cores process the previous block.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook is fire—I definitely feel the pain of paying for H100s and not using them. The chef analogy in Beat 2 is actually solid and not cringe. However, you lost me at 'warp-specialization.' You didn't explain what a warp is, so I'm just nodding along without actually knowing the mechanism. Also, you mention the Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) in Beat 4, but don't explain why that's different from standard memory access, which is the whole point of the speedup.
